main_text.head: JOH. FORBESII SCOTO-BRITANNI ODA Ad Clarissimum Virum: Dn. M. JOH. PHILIPPVM PAREUM: Dav. Fil. Poëtam Laureatum: & Sacri Palatij ac Consistorij Imperialis Vice-Comitem Palatinum: Illustris Scholæ Neostadiensis Rectorem.
main_text.p: QVI tibi par esse volet, PAREE, Ille terreni haud capiatur oris Punctuli angustis: superet necesse est Vertice nubes.
Sæpe te Pindi juga transvolantem, Sæpe Parnassi volucri vehentem Pallados curru, gelidúmq; sæpe Suspicit Hæmum.
O novem turbâ quoties sororum Vidit in notis comitante ripis, Rhenus, agnatúmq; NICER, Deúmq; Haidelus aula!
Tu nites intra patrios, & extra Limites, magno celeber Parente, Quà Deus mundum beat, & triumphat Lampade mundus.
Gloria hæc magni Patris in recentem Transfit ramum: neq; dignus hæres Deficis tanti decoris, PAREE, Nate PAREO.
Et tui splendor procul in remotas Nominis terras penetravit: oris Lacteo quondam est hilarata rivo Gallia felix.

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page is present at the right; the ode's first line and some Greek-free italics are set in italic type throughout the verse. Doubtful: "Deúmq;", "Haidelus", "Nicer" read as printed. The woodcut ornament is not transcribed.
